notes: Capital of the Roman Empire; supreme hub of all Italian road networks. Origin point of the Milliarium Aureum (Golden Milestone).
Principal harbour of Rome at the Tiber mouth; key node for maritime-to-terrestrial traffic transfer. Via Ostiensis terminus.
Most important city of Campania; major junction on the Via Appia and Via Latina; key military and commercial hub.
Largest Greek-founded city in Campania; important cultural and commercial centre. Connected to Capua and Puteoli by road.
Major port on the Bay of Naples; chief harbour for eastern Mediterranean trade until Ostia expanded under Claudius.
Prosperous Campanian coastal town; destroyed 79 CE (Vesuvius). Included as representative Campanian road-network node.
Ancient Oscan and Roman colony; important road junction east of Neapolis linking Campania to Apulia.
Prosperous Roman town destroyed 79 CE; well-documented road connections along the Campanian coastal route.
Terminus of the Via Appia and Via Traiana; primary embarkation point for Greece and the Eastern Mediterranean. Key strategic port.
Major Greek colony turned Roman municipium; important harbour on the Gulf of Taranto. Junction of routes through southern Italy.
Latin colony on Via Appia; strategic crossroads between Apulia and Lucania. Birthplace of Horace.
Important Latin colony in northern Apulia; road junction on routes through the Apennine passes toward the Adriatic.
Greek colony at the tip of Italy; southern terminus of the Via Popilia; embarkation point for Sicily. Extreme southern road endpoint.
Chief Bruttian city; important road junction on the Via Popilia through the toe of Italy toward Rhegium.
Greek and Lucanian city on the Ionian coast; junction linking coastal Lucanian route with interior roads.
Critical road junction: meeting point of Via Appia, Via Traiana, and Via Latina. Major Samnite and Roman colony.
Latin colony in Samnium; important strategic garrison point controlling interior Apennine routes.
Major Adriatic port; northern terminus of the Via Flaminia. Junction linking Adriatic coastal traffic to interior.
Principal city of Picenum; road junction on routes connecting the Adriatic coast to the Apennine interior.
Key colony on the Via Flaminia between Rome and Ariminum. Important military road junction controlling the Apennine pass.
Latin colony on the Via Flaminia immediately north of Rome; first major stop on the road north.
Important Umbrian city; road junction connecting the Via Flaminia to secondary routes through northern Umbria.
Roman colony at a key Arno river crossing; road junction connecting Via Cassia and Via Flaminia corridors.
Major Etruscan and Roman city; junction on the Via Cassia with roads east to Umbrrian towns. Important ceramic production centre.
Major Etruscan city and Roman municipium; road junction linking Etruria to Umbria across the Tiber valley.
Coastal Etruscan and Roman city; important harbour at the Arno mouth on the Via Aurelia corridor.
Major junction on the Via Aemilia; principal road city of Cisalpine Gaul crossing the Apennines toward Etruria.
Latin colony on the Via Aemilia; key road centre in the Po plain between Bononia and Placentia.
Latin colony on the Via Aemilia; important road and commercial node in the Po plain.
Latin colony at the terminus of the Via Aemilia on the Po; major junction connecting to Mediolanum, Genua, and Cremona.
Latin colony at the junction of Via Flaminia (from Rome) and Via Aemilia (north-west); strategic road node on the Adriatic.
Major Ligurian port; junction of coastal Via Aurelia and interior routes over the Apennines toward Placentia (Via Postumia).
Ligurian Roman colony; road junction in the Tanaro valley connecting the Po plain with Alpine routes.
Critical northeastern gateway of Italy; major road hub connecting Italy to the Balkans, Danube frontier, and the Amber Road.
Major road junction on the Adige; connecting Via Postumia with routes north through the Brenner Pass toward Raetia.
Wealthy Venetian city on the Via Postumia; one of the most prosperous cities in Roman Italy.
Important Adriatic port and road junction near Aquileia; gateway to Histria and the Dalmatian coast.
Latin colony on the Po; road junction on Via Postumia linking Genua to Aquileia through the Po plain.
Capital of Transpadana; supreme road hub of northern Italy connecting routes to all Alpine passes and major Po plain cities. Later imperial capital of the West.
Roman colony at the foot of the Alps; road junction controlling Mont Cenis and Little St. Bernard passes into Gaul.
Road junction on the Ticino river; connecting Mediolanum with Placentia and routes south across the Apennines.
Road junction between Mediolanum and Augusta Taurinorum; controlling western Transpadana.
Capital of the Italian allies during the Social War (91–87 BCE); interior road junction in the central Apennines. Pleiades ID: 413063.
Important Latin colony on the Via Latina corridor between Rome and Capua; wine-producing region.
Latin colony on the Tyrrhenian coast of Lucania; road node on the coastal route between Campania and Bruttium.
